title: Introduce pull-generator streaming facade; auth prefetch window and typed backpressure hints; cross-SDK version bumps
author: Maya Gupta
description: Context: multiple SDK consumers requested a compact pull-generator style streaming facade that behaves consistently across Python/TypeScript/Go while giving app developers explicit backpressure hints and predictable auth prefetch for mobile/bandwidth-constrained clients. Motivation: previous async iterator shims had subtle differences (cursor semantics, resume timing, and token refresh jitter) that resulted in inconsistent retry behavior and duplicated code in integrations. This PR introduces a thin "pull-generator" facade in the redwood runtime and coordinated ergonomic adapters and version bumps for the three SDKs; it also adds an auth prefetch window (default 30s) to reduce mid-stream reauth failures and surfaces typed backpressure hint metadata for clients to act on (buffered_bytes, suggested_yield_ms). Changes: 1) runtime: add pull-generator protocol adapter and an opt-in header (X-Stream-Mode: pull) plus small protocol handshake to advertise credential-window and backpressure hints; 2) auth: implement a token prefetch scheduler that initiates refresh at credential_ttl - prefetch_window; expose prefetch_window in session metadata and server-side tracing; 3) SDKs: add compact PullStream facade in Python/TS/Go that normalizes resume/ack semantics, prefetch TTL hint consumption, and exposes a typed backpressure metadata object on each chunk; 4) docs: update streaming.md with examples for mobile and long-lived sessions; 5) tests: add integration tests that simulate slow consumers and auth TTL expiry; 6) versioning: bump Python to 1.19.0, TS to 1.28.1, Go to 1.8.3 to pick up ergonomic APIs. Rollout: feature is behind a feature-flag (runtime:pull_generator_enabled=false by default) while we collect telemetry. Checklist: - [x] runtime adapter implemented and unit-tested - [x] auth prefetch logic covered with unit tests and tracing - [x] Python/TS/Go PullStream facades implemented with docs - [x] integration tests for resume and reauth scenarios - [x] release notes and upgrade guidance drafted Impact: reduces mid-stream auth failures in tests from ~2.3% to <0.5% for TTLs between 60-90s under simulated jitter; provides consumers explicit signals to implement cooperative backpressure without changing underlying streaming transport. Related: references ENG-1429 design doc (link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1429/pull-generator-streaming-proposal) and a support ticket SUP-4472 describing a production incident where short-lived credentials caused mid-stream disconnects.

release_notes: Added PullStream facade (Python/TS/Go) that normalizes streaming resume semantics, introduces a configurable auth prefetch window to reduce mid-stream reauth failures, and surfaces typed backpressure hints. SDKs bumped (py 1.19.0, ts 1.28.1, go 1.8.3). Runtime feature gated behind pull_generator_enabled. Upgrade guidance: consumers should start by toggling the PullStream facade in the SDKs; if you rely on custom transport metadata, verify BackpressureHint compatibility.
upgrade_instructions: 1) For runtime operators: enable runtime feature flag runtime:pull_generator_enabled=true to start serving pull-mode streams. 2) For SDK consumers: update to the new SDK versions (Python 1.19.0, TypeScript 1.28.1, Go 1.8.3) and migrate calls from stream_iterator to PullStream by following docs/streaming.md example. 3) If you use short-lived credentials, consider increasing prefetch_window via client session config (default 30s).
